content:
# Disagreement Log — 2 Maccabees Chapter 13
**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Total Disagreements:** 14

---

## V.3 — "with much hypocrisy" vs. "great show of enthusiasm" vs. "flattering"
- EMET: "with much hypocrisy" (literal *meta pollēs hypokriseos*)
- LOGOS: "with a great show of enthusiasm" (interpretive paraphrase)
- PNEUMA: "flattering" (single word — significant reduction)
- SOPHIA: EMET — "with much hypocrisy" is the correct literal rendering and theologically pointed

## V.4 — "roused the passion" vs. "stirred up Antiochus's anger" vs. "turned Antiochus's fury"
- EMET: "roused the passion"
- LOGOS: "stirred up the anger"
- PNEUMA: "turned the fury"
- SOPHIA: LOGOS — "stirred up anger" captures Greek *parōxynen*: provoked/stirred up

## V.5 — Tower description: "rim running round it that on all sides inclines precipitously" vs. "rim...that slopes precipitously inward"
- EMET: "inclines precipitously into the ashes"
- LOGOS: "slopes precipitously inward toward the ashes"
- PNEUMA: "slopes sharply inward over the ashes"
- SOPHIA: LOGOS phrasing — most precise

## V.6 — "push anyone guilty of sacrilege...to his destruction" vs. "is thrust to destruction" vs. "is shoved...and pushed to their death"
- EMET: "push...to his destruction"
- LOGOS: "is thrust to destruction"
- PNEUMA: "is shoved in...and pushed to their death" (paraphrase)
- SOPHIA: LOGOS phrasing — concise

## V.7 — "Menelaus the lawbreaker met his end" — all three agree
- Slight variation: EMET "met his end" / LOGOS "met his end" / PNEUMA "died"
- SOPHIA: "met his end" — EMET/LOGOS; the Greek *telos elaben* has an ironic finality

## V.8 — "and indeed quite justly" vs. "and justly so" vs. "Fitting, really"
- EMET: "and indeed quite justly"
- LOGOS: "and justly so"
- PNEUMA: "Fitting, really" (colloquial)
- SOPHIA: "And justly so" — LOGOS; concise and formal

## V.11 — "blasphemous Gentiles" vs. "blasphemous Gentiles" vs. "godless pagans"
- EMET/LOGOS: "blasphemous Gentiles"
- PNEUMA: "godless pagans" (loses *blasphēmois*: blasphemers)
- SOPHIA: EMET/LOGOS — the specific term "blasphemous" matters

## V.12 — prostration duration — all three agree: three days
- Slight variation in construction: EMET "lying prostrate for three days without ceasing" / LOGOS same / PNEUMA "lay face down on the ground for three days"
- SOPHIA: LOGOS phrasing

## V.14 — "fight nobly to the death for the laws" vs. "fight nobly to the death for the law" vs. "fight bravely to the death for the law"
- EMET: "laws" (plural)
- LOGOS/PNEUMA: "law" (singular)
- SOPHIA: "law" — Greek *nomōn* is genitive plural but the reference is to Torah as a single concept; "law" is standard

## V.15 — "watchword" vs. "watchword" vs. (implied)
- EMET/LOGOS: "watchword" explicitly
- PNEUMA: "gave his men the watchword" then quotes — same meaning
- All three agree on "God's victory" as the watchword

## V.15 — "stabbed the leading elephant along with the man upon it" vs. "ran through the lead elephant together with its mahout" vs. "ran a sword through the lead elephant and its rider"
- LOGOS uses "mahout" — unnecessarily technical; Greek *ton ep' autou*: the one on it
- SOPHIA: "the man on it" — EMET/PNEUMA phrasing preferred over "mahout"

## V.22 — "gave his hand in pledge" vs. "gave his right hand as pledge" vs. "shook hands on an agreement"
- EMET: "gave his hand in pledge"
- LOGOS: "gave his right hand as pledge" — *dexian dous*: giving the right hand (a formal pledge gesture)
- PNEUMA: "shook hands on an agreement" (anachronistic casualness)
- SOPHIA: LOGOS — "gave his right hand as pledge"

## V.23 — textual difficulty; all three diverge
- EMET: conflates several actions without clear sequence
- LOGOS: most coherent narrative sequence
- PNEUMA: adds "He was shaken" as narrator interpolation
- SOPHIA: LOGOS structure but retains "swore" explicitly

## V.26 — "mounted the public platform" vs. "went up to the public platform" vs. "got up on the platform"
- EMET: "mounted"
- LOGOS: "went up to"
- PNEUMA: "got up on" (colloquial)
- SOPHIA: "mounted the public platform" — EMET phrasing; "mounted" has appropriate formality
